desc:
For each index i of nums, define its second greater value as follows: among the positions to the right of i, look at those holding a value strictly larger than nums[i]; the second greater value is the value at the second such position, counted from left to right. If fewer than two such positions exist, it is -1.

Return an array with the second greater value of every index.

Example: nums = [2, 4, 0, 9, 6] gives [9, 6, 6, -1, -1]. For the 2, the larger values to its right are 4, 9, 6 in that order, so the second is 9. For the 4, they are 9 and 6, so the second is 6.
hints: The ordinary next greater element uses one stack. What if an element needs to be 'beaten' twice before it is settled?
Keep two groups of waiting indices: those that have not yet seen any greater value, and those that have seen exactly one and now wait for a second.

For each new value x: first pop from the second group every index whose value is < x and answer it with x. Then move every index of the first group with value < x into the second group (keeping their relative order so the second group stays sorted), and finally push the current index on the first group.
editorial: Use two monotonic stacks of indices: s1 holds indices that have seen no greater value yet, and s2 holds indices that have seen exactly one. Both keep their values non-increasing from bottom to top. When a value x arrives:

(1) Settle second-group indices: while the top of s2 has a value < x, pop it and set its answer to x (this is the second larger value it meets). Do this first, so that an index promoted in step 2 is not settled by the same x. (2) Promote first-group indices: pop everything from s1 with a value < x; these have now seen one greater value. Push them onto s2 in their original order (reverse of the pop order) so that s2 stays non-increasing. (3) Push the current index on s1.
Every index enters each stack once and leaves once, so time is O(n) and space is O(n). Indices still waiting at the end keep the answer -1.
solution:
def secondGreater(nums):
    n = len(nums)
    answer = [-1] * n
    first = []   # indices that have seen no greater value yet
    second = []  # indices that have seen exactly one greater value
    for j, x in enumerate(nums):
        while second and nums[second[-1]] < x:
            answer[second.pop()] = x
        moved = []
        while first and nums[first[-1]] < x:
            moved.append(first.pop())
        second.extend(reversed(moved))
        first.append(j)
    return answer
